questions.q: Which six operations make up the Apex DML statements?
options: select, insert, update, delete, grant, revoke
insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, merge
create, read, update, destroy, archive, restore
save, load, sync, push, pull, merge
questions.explain: The DML statements are insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, and merge.

questions.q: By default, what does `upsert` use to decide whether to insert a new record or update an existing one?
options: The record's Name field
The record's own Id field, unless a different field is explicitly specified
The order the records appear in the list
Whichever field is marked required in page layout
questions.explain: upsert matches on the record's Id by default; you can pass a specific external ID field as a second argument instead.

questions.q: Which four standard objects support the `merge` statement?
options: Account, Contact, Case, and Lead
Account, Opportunity, Quote, and Order
Contact, Task, Event, and Note
Any custom object with an external ID field
questions.explain: merge combines up to three duplicate records and is only available for Account, Contact, Case, and Lead.

questions.q: What happens if one record out of five fails validation inside a single `insert` DML statement on a list?
options: The four valid records are saved and the fifth is skipped silently
Only the fifth record fails; the other four are unaffected either way
The whole statement throws a DmlException and none of the five records are saved
Apex automatically retries the failing record with default values
questions.explain: A plain DML statement is all-or-nothing: if any record fails, a DmlException is thrown and nothing in that statement is committed.

options: Permanently removes acct from the Recycle Bin
Restores a previously deleted record (identified by its Id) out of the Recycle Bin
Reverts the most recent field update on acct
Cancels a pending insert before it commits
questions.explain: undelete restores a deleted record from the Recycle Bin, using the Id already on the sObject variable.
